doc_name: List of Ig Nobel Prize winners
text: The Ig Nobel Prizes are a parody of the Nobel Prizes, awarded each year in mid-September—around the same time as the genuine Nobel Prizes are announced—for ten achievements that "first make people laugh, and then make them think." These prizes are intended to celebrate the unusual, honor imaginative work, and spur public interest in science, medicine, and technology. All awards recognize real achievements, except for three in 1991 and one in 1994, which were due to an erroneous press release. The awards ceremony has taken place on various dates, including 6 October 1995, 3 October 1996, 9 October 1997, 8 October 1998, 30 September 1999, 5 October 2000, 4 October 2001, 3 October 2002, 2 October 2003, 30 September 2004, 6 October 2005, 5 October 2006, 4 October 2007, 2 October 2008, 1 October 2009, 30 September 2010, 29 September 2011, 20 September 2012, 12 September 2013, 18 September 2014, 17 September 2015 at Harvard's Sanders Theatre (the 25th First Annual ceremony), 22 September 2016, 14 September 2017, 13 September 2018, 12 September 2019, 17 September 2020 (webcast), 9 September 2021 (31st First Annual, webcast), 15 September 2022 (32nd First Annual, webcast), 14 September 2023 (33rd First Annual, webcast), 12 September 2024 (34th First Annual, held at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology), and 18 September 2025 (35th First Annual, held at Boston University). Each winner receives a medal shaped like a frying pan that makes noise when shaken and Cambridge parking passes valid from 3 a.m. to 4 a.m. the day after Christmas. The first nomination also included three fictional recipients for fictional achievements.
